propositions: The outbound mapper receives its assignee resolver via attribute injection (`_assignee_resolver`) wrapped in silent try-except, causing authoritative resolution to fail invisibly if injection stops happening.

The attribute-injection pattern hides bugs in review: the Data Center adapter copied the getattr discovery into a class where the attribute was never set, making an entire authoritative branch dead code.
The injected attribute is invisible to the type checker and requires `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` at multiple sites, violating type contract clarity.
Resolvers must be threaded explicitly as declared keyword-only parameters on the neutral `OutboundMapper.resolve_assignee` port and both implementers (Cloud and DC backends).

DC's constructor-bound resolver (per-client, no jira_key) must coexist with the core's per-issue resolver (from compute_update_fields), with explicit parameter taking precedence to preserve today's overwrite semantics.

The resolver must be threaded through `diff_canonical_fields` from `compute_update_fields` to the `resolve_assignee` call site, and all attribute-injection blocks and `getattr` discovery patterns must be deleted.
